Pakistan’s inflation rate is projected to rise to 9.9% in 2027, while economic growth is expected to ease to 3.5%, according to data released by the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF)World Economic Outlook (WEO)released on Tuesday.

The IMF data showed inflation at 7.1% in 2026, up from 4.5% in 2025. Pakistan’s gross domestic product (GDP) growth is projected at 3.6% in 2026, compared with 3.2% in 2025, before moderating to 3.5% in 2027.

According to theWEO, Pakistan’s current account balance is projected to remain flat in 2026 before slipping into a deficit equivalent to 1% of GDP in 2027, compared with a surplus of 0.5% of GDP in 2025.

Moreover, the country’s unemployment rate is forecast to decline to 6.9% in 2026 and 6.5% in 2027, from 7.1% in 2025, the data showed.

As per the report, global growth is projected to slow to 3.1% in 2026 and rebound to 3.4% in 2027. Global headline inflation is projected to rise notably to 4.7% in 2026 before easing to 4.1% in 2027.

The outlook noted that the global economy is again proving resilient, but unevenly so and with rapidly narrowing margins of adjustment in the near term.

“Activity in the first half of 2026 held up better than expected despite the dragging war in the Middle East and continuing strains from trade tensions.

“The technology cycle has provided a demand impulse, driven by strong investment in artificial intelligence (AI).

“The interaction of these forces—geopolitics and technology—has produced a split global economy: Favourable terms of trade or technology-related exports and investment give some countries a cushion, whereas others face higher import bills and weaker demand.

“Use of buffers and adaptability have helped economies weather the negative shocks so far. Flexible supply responses, rerouting of shipments, inventory drawdowns, fiscal support measures, and lower energy intensity than in previous decades have helped contain the hit to activity from the war.”

According to the outlook, energy-importing economies outside the technology value chain face the most difficult outlook. But the margins of adjustment that helped resilience are not limitless, and risks are skewed to the downside.

Further escalation in conflicts, a reassessment of expectations surrounding AI, renewed trade tensions, and fiscal vulnerabilities could weaken growth. On the upside, stronger momentum in AI investment and productivity gains from AI or a sustained easing of geopolitical and trade tensions could strengthen growth, read the report.

ISLAMABAD: Tax advisers, consultants, tax experts and chartered accountants have requested the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) chairman to further extend date by November 15, 2026 keeping in view genuine concerns.

In a communication to FBR Chairman on Monday, Javed Iqbal Qazi, Advocate Supreme Court and Chairman of the Pakistan Tax Advisers Association, requested for extension in time for filing of Income Tax returns/Wealth statements for the Tax Year 2026 which falls due on 15.10.2026.

Due to financial constraints/crises in country, very slow functioning of IRIS system, load-shedding problems being faced in different areas of the country and heavy burden on tax practitioners, advocates and chartered accountants the target fixed for number of returns cannot be achieved by October 15, 2026.

At present about 60-65 percent of the work has been completed by all tax practitioners and target fixed by the FBR will not be achieved by 15.10.2026.

The quantum of returns required to be filed by the taxpayers through the above noted three categories of the tax practitioners is too heavy and requires lot of time for the preparation of returns, as new columns have been inserted in the return forms which require lot of time for submission of the same, deposit of tax through CPRNS in the banks and submission on IRIS system.

The Pakistan Tax Advisers Association has received many massages from our members throughout the country to help the taxpayers/tax practitioners for the redressal of the genuine demand of the public at large and to achieve the financial targets fixed by FBR on the following grounds.

i) That manual return for low-income taxpayers has not been uploaded as yet on IRIS system.

ii) That the functioning of IRIS portal is very slow and takes too much time for uploading of the return which has been made too lengthy and tedious.

iii) That the financial position of the taxpayers have not allowed them to deposit their tax liability in the government exchequer in time.

Javed Iqbal Qazi has requested the FBR chairman that in the interest of justice and fair play, it is prayed that the taxpayers, the tax practitioners be facilitated and the last date of submission of returns be extended upto November 15, 2026.

BEIJING: China’s central bank stepped up its gold purchases in September, extending its buying streak to a 23rd consecutive month, official data showed on Wednesday.

Gold holdings by the People’s Bank of China rose to 77.47 million fine troy ounces at the end of September from 76.73 million ounces a month earlier. China has continued to accumulate gold despite sharp swings in bullion prices this year.

The value of China’s gold reserves fell to USD323.52 billion at the end of September from USD350.08 billion a month earlier, the data showed. Gold prices fell over 6percent in September. Spot gold was most recently trading at around USD4,147.47 per ounce on Wednesday at 0244 GMT.

The FBR proposes expanding income tax rules from YouTube to all social media platforms by amending existing provisions, aiming to broaden the digital tax framework for online content creators.

article_text:
The FBR proposes expanding income tax rules from YouTube to all social media platforms by amending existing provisions, aiming to broaden the digital tax framework for online content creators.

ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has proposed expanding the scope of income tax rules from YouTube to all social media platforms, potentially bringing a wider range of online content creators and digital platforms within the existing tax framework.

The FBR has drafted notifications proposing amendments to the Income Tax Rules, 2002, replacing the word “YouTube” with “social media platforms” in two separate provisions dealing with income tax.

Under the first proposed amendment, the FBR seeks to revise clause (d) of sub-rule (1) of rule 13ZP in Chapter IIA of the Income Tax Rules, 2002. The amendment is being proposed under section 99C, read with sub-section (1) of section 237 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001.

The second draft notification proposes a similar change in clause (d) of sub-rule (1) of rule 19R in Chapter VA of the Income Tax Rules, 2002. This amendment is proposed under section 99C, read with clause (b) of sub-section (3B) of section 101 and sub-section (1) of section 237 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001.

By replacing the platform-specific reference to YouTube with the broader term “social media platforms”, the proposed changes could extend the relevant provisions beyond YouTube to other social media services.

The FBR has invited objections and suggestions from all persons likely to be affected by the proposed amendments. Stakeholders have been given seven days from publication of the draft notifications in the official Gazette to submit their feedback for consideration by the Board.

The notifications state that objections and suggestions received within the prescribed period will be considered by the FBR before proceeding further.

The proposed amendments remain at the draft stage and do not, by themselves, establish that the changes have been finalised or brought into force.

ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday directed the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to complete the digital monitoring system of sales production in major industries by the end of December, as part of efforts to narrow the gap between actual and potential tax collection.

Chairing a meeting in Islamabad to review FBR reforms, the premier instructed tax authorities to ensure production monitoring for sales tax across all manufacturing sectors by the year end, an official statement said.

It added that officials gave a detailed presentation to the premier on the results achieved so far from the industries already under the monitoring system.

The meeting was informed that the digital monitoring system had been fully installed in sugar, cement, tobacco, tiles and fertilisers sectors. The monitoring system was in the process of being installed in the textile, packaged water, packaged juice, and packaged milk sectors, and the purchase of equipment for this purpose had been completed, the meeting was told.

It was further informed that the purchase of equipment for the sectors of steel, poultry, and tires will be completed by Oct 15, while for tea, household electronics, leather, paper and board, and oil and ghee, the purchase will be completed by Oct 30.

As a result, the monitoring systems in all these production sectors are expected to be fully operational by Dec 31, it was told.

The meeting was informed that in the textile sector, some industries had shown resistance to the installation of the monitoring system. However, Nishat Mills, Al-Karam Textile, Al-Karam Cotton Mills, J.K. Spinning Mills, Soorti Enterprises, Interloop Limited, Faisal Spinning Mills, Ibrahim Fibers Limited, Sapphire Textiles Limited and Nishat Chunian had voluntarily installed the monitoring system in compliance with government measures.

PM Shehbaz appreciated these companies for their cooperation.

A review report on the gap between actual and potential tax collection was also presented to the premier, which provided an estimate of the country’s tax potential and assessed additional revenue that could potentially be generated via improved tax compliance and enforcement.

The meeting was informed that due to government measures over the past three years, an additional Rs1.3 trillion in tax had beencollected— a 40 per cent increase in tax collection. This additional tax was collected due to enforcement measures, it was told.

During its briefing, the FBR said that production monitoring was being made effective with the help of cameras under the faceless system.

“The prime minister directed the removal of all hurdles in the installation of automated production monitoring systems,” the statement said.

He also noted that businesses collecting and pocketing taxes from consumers themselves instead of depositing it into the national exchequer were not entitled to any concessions.

The premier said that those businesses in the production sector that were voluntarily installing the monitoring system were viewed with appreciation. He added that all necessary measures would be taken to achieve the country’s “full tax potential” and ensure effective enforcement of tax laws.

He commended the FBR Transformation Team for its “round-the-clock efforts” in preparing the comprehensive assessment and identifying the gap between potential revenue and actual collection. He also appreciated the officials involved in preparing the report, presenting them with shields after the meeting.

The prime minister said that to assess the effectiveness of the production monitoring system, the IT ministry should also conduct audits in other sectors. He termed the collection of tax in accordance with the country’s full tax potential a “true service to the public”.

The meeting was attended by Federal Ministers Azam Nazeer Tarar, Dr Musadik Malik, Ahad Khan Cheema and Shaza Fatima Khawaja, as well as Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani, Advisor to the Prime Minister Haroon Akhtar, and relevant senior officials.

The government on Monday reduced the price of petrol by Rs2.93 per litre, but increased that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.61 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs395.37 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.85 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 13 (Tuesday).

The price of HSD has come down from apeak of Rs520.35recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price hadpeaked at Rs458.41on April 3 after beginning itsupward trajectoryfrom Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government hasreintroduceda raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malikannouncedthat fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcingweekly revisionsto fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April alsoannouncedtargeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

ISLAMABAD: Pakis­tan could realise economic benefits of $60 billion to $80bn over the next five years through digital transformation, with agriculture, real estate and healthcare expected to gain significantly.

A working paper issued by the Pakistan Digital Authority (PDA) says digitalisation is a major opportunity to accelerate economic growth, improve public service delivery, and streamline government operations.

The working paper has been forwarded to the Ministry of IT & Telecom. However, it notes that the lack of interoperability among government digital systems remains a significant challenge.

The paper adds that digital transformation could generate more than $9bn in economic benefits for the agriculture sector by 2030, while digital reforms in healthcare could yield savings of over $450m.

The real estate sector could attract an additional $15bn in investment by 2030 through digital transformation, the document states. Under the proposed digital framework, the authority will help develop a National Digital Master Plan and digital infrastructure to improve coordination between federal and provincial governments.

The National Digital Master Plan will focus on integrating government systems, reducing administrative bottlenecks and establishing common digital standards across public-sector institutions.

The proposed Pakistan Digital Stack will bring together digital identity, payment systems, and data-exchange mechanisms to enable seamless, secure interactions among government departments.

headline: Pakistan’s poverty rate higher than India, Bangladesh, UNDP says

article_text:
WASHINGTON: More than one-third of Pakistan’s population faces overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards, according to the United Nations Development Prog­ramme’s (UNDP) Multidimensional Pov­er­ty Index (MPI) released on Monday.

Figures released by the UNDP in New York show that 38.3 per cent of Pakistan’s population was multidimensionally poor, compared with 16.4 per cent in India and 14.9pc in Bangladesh. The estimates are based on household surveys conducted in different years and do not provide a strictly contemporaneous comparison.

In Pakistan, the intensity of deprivation among those classified as multidimensionally poor stood at 51.7pc. Another 12.9pc of the population was considered vulnerable to multidimensional poverty, indicating that a substantial share of people remained at risk of falling into acute deprivation.

Unlike conventional income-based measures, the MPI assesses overlapping disadvantages in areas such as nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, school attendance, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing and household assets.

UNDP estimates 38.3pc Pakistanis face multidimensional poverty

The report also documents a worrying global reversal. The number of people living in multidimensional poverty has risen for the first time in 15 years, reaching 1.2 billion, as families struggle to meet their basic needs.

The latest total is 51.5 million higher than the previous update. Children account for more than half of those affected, with 617m living in multidimensional poverty, while 83pc of the total live in rural areas.

The global findings underline the scale of the challenge facing governments, particularly in providing essential services to disadvantaged communities. Poverty is not simply a shortage of income; it can also mean inadequate nutrition, missed schooling and a lack of clean water or electricity.

South Asia accounts for a substantial share of global deprivation. The report says the region accounts for at least one-third of global deprivations in nutrition, housing, and years of schooling.

It is also home to 150m poor people living in households where a school-aged child is not attending school, highlighting persistent barriers to education despite broader development gains.

The UNDP’s regional figures put South Asia’s multidimensional poverty rate at approximately 19.3pc, with another 18.4pc of the population vulnerable to such poverty. Health accounts for about 29.9pc of the contribution to regional multidimensional poverty, education for 33.7pc and living standards for 36.3pc.

The figures show how disadvantages in different areas reinforce one another. Poor health, inadequate education and substandard living conditions can trap families in poverty and make it difficult for them to improve their circumstances.

“The rise in poverty should be a wake-up call for the world,” said UNDP Administrator Alexander De Croo.

“Behind these figures are 1.2 billion people facing hardships that reinforce one another: hunger, missed schooling and a lack of clean water or electricity. This is unacceptable.”

ISLAMABAD: The government said on Monday it had to cut the foreign-funded project portfolio by more than half, from Rs537 billion to Rs255bn, due to a shortage of matching funds in local currency for the current fiscal year.

This was reported to the Senate Standing Committee on Planning, Development and Special Initiatives by a team led by Planning Secretary Dr Tahir Noor.

Mr Noor also informed the committee that work on the Sukkur-Hyderabad (M6) Motorway would begin “within months” as foreign financing totalling $705 million was now available.

The meeting, presided over by Senator Quratulain Marri, reviewed allocations for foreign-funded development projects under PSDP 2026–27.

The panel was informed that 98 foreign-funded projects, with a total estimated cost of Rs8.1 trillion, were included in the current fiscal year’s PSDP, involving foreign assistance of Rs4.65tr.

Against a demand of Rs537bn for rupee cover, the Economic Affairs Division (EAD) had proposed Rs425bn after consultation with the ministries, divisions and donor agencies concerned. However, the National Economic Council (NEC), while approving the PSDP at Rs1tr against an overall demand of Rs2.9tr on June 10, allocated only Rs255bn for these projects due to fiscal constraints.

Senator Marri sought clarification regarding projects expected to be completed during the current financial year. The planning team reported that most of the projects were expected to be completed during the year.

The Senate committee emphasised effective monitoring and timely implementation to achieve projected targets for projects that were now at an advanced stage.

While reviewing the need for reliance on foreign loans, particularly dollar-denominated financing carrying interest and repayment obligations, the panel was of the view that priority should be given to domestic resources and rupee allocations because foreign borrowing had financial implications and needed to be carefully assessed. The government should explore the effective utilisation of local resources to reduce unnecessary dependence on external loans, the panel observed.

The committee was of the view that foreign-funded projects must receive adequate rupee cover to avoid implementation delays, while ensuring transparency, accountability, prudent financial management and coordination with donor agencies.

It emphasised balancing foreign as­­sis­tance with domestic fiscal capacity and mi­­nimising avoidable financial burdens.

The meeting reviewed progress on the Sukkur–Hyderabad Motorway project and expressed concern over prolonged delays. The committee was told that Sections I and II were being processed under the public-private partn­ership (PPP) mode, with the concession award targeted for February next year.

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has agreed to provide transaction advisory services for these sections.

In addition, financing arrangements with international development partners had been secured for the remaining sections, the planning ministry reported.

ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Sheh­baz Sharif on Monday directed the auth­orities to increase financing for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) from Rs1.1 trillion to Rs2.2tr by 2028, citing their potential to drive economic growth and create business opportunities across the country.

Presiding over a meeting on the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (Smeda), the prime minister said the business community was the backbone of any country’s economy, while Pakistan’s SME sector had imme­nse potential to accelerate economic dev­elopment, according to a press release issued by the Prime Minister’s Office.

He said ongoing reforms at Smeda ai­­m­­ed to empower small and medium-siz­­ed entrepreneurs and facilitate the esta­blishment and expansion of businesses.

The prime minister emphasised the need to empower people in underdeveloped areas, saying this would help red­uce migration to major cities and contribute to balanced national development.

PM Shehbaz directed Smeda to formulate a comprehensive plan to educate more people about the procedures for obtaining business loans and take effective measures to raise awareness about entrepreneurship.

Feasibility studies

He also instructed the authority to commission feasibility studies for setting up SMEs in various sectors with the help of relevant industry experts and make them available in local languages. The initiative, he said, would enable aspiring entrepreneurs across the country to benefit from the studies.

During the meeting, the prime minister was briefed on ongoing reforms at Smeda and measures to promote the SME sector.

The meeting was informed that Smeda was being transformed into a central platform to train aspiring entrepreneurs and facilitate their access to bank financing for setting up businesses.

Smeda offices were being established across the country to improve outreach and access to services, while the authority was developing an artificial intelligence-based helpline to provide information and guidance to citizens in local languages. The meeting was also informed that a memorandum of understanding had been signed between global e-commerce company Alibaba and Smeda under which 10,000 SMEs would receive training over two years.

Officials said reforms were also under way to improve the effectiveness and user-friendliness of Smeda’s digital portal.

Daanish IT Park

At a separate meeting, PM Shehbaz directed the authorities concerned to develop the Daanish IT Park Islamabad into a world-class technology hub and a centre for a modern IT ecosystem through effective collaboration between academia and industry.

He said the government would continue efforts to equip Pakistani youth with modern skills in information technology, artificial intelligence and financial technology, while creating new opportunities for IT entrepreneurs.

He instructed the Ministry of Information Technology to conduct a comprehensive case study of the project and directed the authorities to make the IT park operational in partnership with global technology companies. He also ordered a third-party audit of the project.

The meeting was briefed on plans to create a comprehensive ecosystem to boost IT exports and promote investment in the sector. It was informed that 50 privately owned buildings had been upgraded into software technology parks under the Pakistan Software Export Board.

Additionally, eight incubation centres had been established across the country to support start-ups, while 105 co-working spaces were operational to facilitate IT professionals.

Participants were told that global technology companies were being approached to help operationalise the Daanish IT Park Islamabad.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) warned on Tuesday that while low-income developing countries were dealing with the disproportionate impacts of theIran war-fuelled energy shock, many had “no choice” but to cut spending or potentially face debt restructuring.

Speaking toAFPon the sidelines of the organisation’s Annual Meetings in Bangkok, IMF deputy director of research, Petya Koeva Brooks, said that the heavily indebted oil-importing countries were facing the worst of the energy shock, and had difficult choices in helping their citizens through the crisis.

“Unfortunately, after years of the global economy being hit [by] shock after shock, debt levels have increased quite a lot, and at the same time, inflation has become a problem,” she said.

TheUS war on Iranhas plunged the Middle East into conflict and sentglobal energy prices soaring, as Tehran’s retaliatory action targeted Washington’s Gulf allies and curtailed oil and gas supplies.

Those prices have begun to bleed into other goods, with the crisis also having an effect on crucial fertiliser supplies.

The IMF has called on countries to offer narrow, targeted subsidies in the wake of the crisis, while also recommending all governments work to rebuild fiscal buffers and address rising debt after years of fighting economic shocks since the pandemic.

“Our messages indeed apply to most countries, but again, the trade-offs and the choices that have to be made are much more difficult for the most vulnerable countries,” Koeva Brooks said.

The IMF’sWorld Economic Outlook, released on Tuesday, identified low-income developing countries that are net oil importers and are not exposed to the ongoing artificial intelligence technology investment boom as being the most vulnerable to the shocks from the Iran war.

“For those countries that are most vulnerable, this is where the consumption basket is heavily weighted towards energy and food, and so indeed it is much much more difficult,” she said.

“But unfortunately there is no other choice.”

The senior IMF official added that “many” low-income countries were in debt distress, or close to it, and that they should seek debt restructuring if they were not able to address the issue.

“Where debt is not sustainable, then resolving that debt and having orderly and timely restructuring is always better than waiting, because then the cost of restructuring down the road is going to be much higher,” she said.

In its World Economic Outlook, the IMF raised its forecast for 2026 global growth, largely on the back of advanced economies enjoying a boost from AI-related investments and economic activity.

Growth outcomes were highly uneven across economies, depending on their exposure to the war and whether they were integrated into AI supply chains.

The world’s advanced economies were forecast to grow 2.1 per cent in 2026, with those in the AI supply chain such as Taiwan and South Korea posting significantly higher figures.

Koeva Brooks toldAFPthat if AI investment activity were to slow, the world economy “would see a negative impact on output, not only in advanced countries like the US but again through trade linkages also in Asia”.

In the IMF’s worst-case scenario — of AI not delivering promised productivity gains — global GDP forecasts for 2028 would fall by as much as 0.4pc.

Climate-related risks were another key part of the World Economic Outlook this year, and Koeva Brooks toldAFPthat some of the effects of a particularly intense El Niño phenomenon had already been taken into account in higher prices for certain food items.

The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Niño raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding, and exacerbate man-made global warming.

“We have a significant increase in beverage prices, in the prices of rice, and so on,” said Koeva Brooks.

“Of course, it could turn out that the domino effect is even bigger than what we currently have.”

NEW YORK: Apple on Tuesday is expected to show off a new round of smart home products, including an iPad-like device meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops that will showcase its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant.

The devices will help users control doorbells, thermostats, and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. The devices could also include upgrades to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices, analysts said.

Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off challenges from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own.

Investors are looking more closely at Apple’s hardware sales for growth as the company’s services revenue has come under regulatory pressure.

Apple cuts iPhone 18 Pro orders due to soft demand, Nikkei Asia reports

Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet’s Google Home speakers and Amazon’s Echo line. Analysts said two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers.

Apple this summer upgraded Siri’s capabilities with assistance from Google, but the process of wiring a smart home is still too difficult for many Apple consumers to see a benefit, said Bob O’Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research.

“Advancements in AI should finally help, but the key questions for Apple are, do they have connectivity smarts to simplify the process, and are they going to be willing to work across the smart home ecosystem and not just within their own walled garden,” O’Donnell said.

Indian benchmark sharesrose on Tuesday, led by the IT index’s biggest one-day gain in more than 17 months after estimate-beating results from HCLTech and as the central bank’s support for the rupee boosted sentiment.

The Nifty 50 rose 1.6% to 22,721.95 and the BSE Sensex added 1.54% to 73,033.78.

The Indian rupee rose to 95.28 per dollar, marking its second consecutive session of recovery, as the Reserve Bank of India announced more measures to alleviate ‌pressure on the currency.

KUALA LUMPUR:Malaysian palm oil futuresreversed earlier losses to hit a more than two-week high on Tuesday, as concerns over tighter supplies next year — due to El Niño and growing biodiesel demand — outweighed pressure from currently high stockpiles.

The benchmark palm oil contract for December delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange rose 45 ringgit, or 0.97%, to 4,682 ringgit ($1,146.43) a metric ton, the highest closing price since September 24.

The bearish September stocks are already reflected in the market as it had already weakened before and after the release of the Malaysian Palm Oil Board’s data, said Cheang Kang Wei, agricultural commodities analyst at the Singapore-based StoneX brokerage.

Malaysia’s palm oil stockpiles in September surged to 3.51 million metric tons as production hit an all-time high, surpassing market expectations and reaching unprecedented levels.

However, Cheang said that the key question now is whether stocks can continue rising in October, noting that inventories could still remain elevated, but the pace of the build should start slowing.

Stock growth should begin moderating by November if exports hold above 1.5 million tons while production stabilises around 2.0 million tons, Cheang added. But if demand disappoints while production remains near record levels, stocks could stay above 3.5 million tons for longer and continue weighing on prices.

“The market is also increasingly looking beyond the current inventory situation and focusing on potential supply risks in 2027, including the lagged impact of El Niño and Indonesia’s growing biodiesel demand under B50,” he said.

Cargo surveyors estimated that exports of Malaysian palm oil products for October 1-10 rose between 33.5% and 37.7% from a month earlier.

Oil prices fell as traders assessed supply risks from attacks on Saudi Arabia while weighing the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia.

Weaker crude oil futures make palm a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

Dalian’s most-active soyoil contract fell 0.65%, while its palm oil contract shed 0.77%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were up 0.55%.

Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

headline: Pakistan’s growth during FY27 projected at 3.5pc, inflation at 9.9pc: IMF

article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has projected Pakistan’s economic growth at 3.5 per cent during the current fiscal year and inflation to remain close to double digits for another year, notwithstanding global growthrebounding to 3.4pc.

In its flagship World Economic Outlook,releasedat the launch of the World Bank-IMF annual meetings in Bangkok, the fund estimated Pakistan’s current account deficit to widen to 1pc of GDP from a surplus of 0.5pc in FY2025. Headline inflation is projected to rise significantly to 9.9pc from 7.1pc last year.

However, the Washington-based lending agency projected Pakistan’s unemployment rate to decline to 6.5pc this year, compared with 6.9pc last year and 7.1pc a year earlier.

The fund, which concluded its review of Pakistan’s economic situation last week, did not explain the projected decline in unemployment despite therising populationand its other economic forecasts, including higher inflation and a widening current account deficit.

The fund’s growth projections are significantly lower than the government’s 4pc target for the current year and the3.8pc forecastby the World Bank last month. Its estimated 3.5pc growth rate for Pakistan is slightly lower than the 3.6pc recorded last year but higher than the 3.2pc in FY2025.

Saying global economic activity had proved resilient despite multiple challenges, the international lender projected global growth to slow to 3.1pc in 2026 before rebounding to 3.4pc in 2027. Global headline inflation is projected to rise notably to 4.7pc in 2026 before easing to 4.1pc in 2027, it added.

The IMF attributed global economic resilience to the technology upturn, buffers and adaptations that helped mitigate the damage from geopolitics-driven disruptions.

“In less than seven years, the global economy has been subjected to an exceptional sequence of events. The pandemic and the ensuing disruptions to global supply chains; the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, with the consequent sharp increases in the prices of energy and other commodities; and significant changes in trade barriers and trading relations have tested the resilience of households, firms, financial markets, and governments,” it said.

“Individually, each of these major developments would have been considered unlikely. Their confluence over such a short period of time is even more extraordinary. Yet, despite this barrage of shocks, the global economy has held up,” the IMF said.

It added that labour markets had remained unexpectedly strong, financial systems had broadly withstood the shocks and the sharpest monetary tightening in half a century, while inflation had receded from its peaks in many economies, although it remained persistent in some cases.

The IMF warned that energy-importing economies like Pakistan, which have limited links to the technology value chain, face the most difficult outlook. The margins of adjustment that have helped sustain resilience, however, are not limitless, and risks are skewed to the downside.

Further escalation in conflicts, a reassessment ofexpectationssurrounding artificial intelligence (AI), renewed trade tensions and fiscal vulnerabilities could weaken growth. On the upside, stronger momentum in AI investment and productivity gains from AI, or a sustained easing of geopolitical and trade tensions, could strengthen growth, it said.

The fund advised its members that fiscal frameworks must deliver better results in dealing with disruptive shocks and build policy space through revenue measures. During cost-of-living crises, governments should preserve price signals and rely primarily on temporary, targeted income support for the most vulnerable, it said.

The stable global aggregate masks a reallocation of growth across economies. Countries with limited direct exposure to the war shock and strong participation in the technology upturn are seeing activity hold up or strengthen. Energy exporters outside the immediate conflict zone are benefiting from favourable terms of trade.

Conversely, energy-importing economies with little connection to the technology value chain face the most difficult combination of higher import costs and exchange rate pressures, weaker real incomes, more constrained fiscal space and fewer offsetting demand impulses.

Many low-income and vulnerable countries belong to this latter group, increasing the risk that recent shocks will widen income gaps across and within countries.

The IMF projected world trade volume growth to slow in 2026 and stabilise in 2027, reflecting the drag from tariffs, adjustments in production chains and continued strength in technology-related trade.

Global imbalances are expected to decline only modestly over the medium term, as large fiscal deficits, limited domestic rebalancing, technology-driven capital flows and differing demand compositions across major economies under current policies continue to sustain external gaps.

The medium-term growth outlook remains lacklustre by historical standards and uneven across countries, partly reflecting varying degrees of AI preparedness and the robustness of energy mixes.

Risks are skewed to the downside, the IMF warned, adding that a prolonged stalemate or furtherescalation in the Middle Eastcould keep energy and food prices elevated and volatile, revive inflationary pressures, worsen fiscal and external balances, and weigh on growth.

Further disruptions to energy infrastructure, cyberattacks or extreme weather events could amplify these effects.

A day earlier, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb toldReutersthat the government expected the economy to growby more than 4pcthis fiscal year despite elevated oil prices. He also said the government was looking to privatise five to six entities during the year, potentially raising more than $1 billion.

Pakistan’s economy remains vulnerable to a prolonged conflict in the Middle East because of its dependence on Gulf energy imports, remittances and financing support from the region.

Copper pricesrose for a third straight session on Tuesday as persistent concerns over a supply shortage kept the metal within striking distance of an all-time peak.

Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.1% at $14,636.50 a metric ton as of 0915 GMT, close to the record $14,875 seen last month.

Supply concerns remained in focus after Chile’s Codelco partially suspended operations at its El Teniente mine following a landslide, while Antofagasta’s Centinela copper mine and two unions were set to resume talks as a strike continued.

“Copper continues to benefit from physical-market tightness and declining exchange inventories, helping it withstand the firm dollar better than the wider complex,” Sucden Financial said in a note.

A stronger greenback makes dollar-denominated metals more expensive for holders of other currencies. The dollar took a breather on Tuesday but hovered near an 18-month high.

All reported copper mine disruptions for 2025-26 — including at Indonesia’s Grasberg mine and Kamoa-Kakula in the Democratic Republic of Congo — amount to 350,000-400,000 tons per year of contained copper, which equates to only 30%-50% of published disruption allowances, Panmure Liberum said.

“Therefore, the dominant price driver is probably speculative/financial,” the bank added in a note.

A disruption allowance is a percentage of mine production that analysts assume will be lost due to unplanned events in a given year.

LME copper stocks declined by 1,625 tons to 232,275 tons, leaving inventories outside the US tight. The cash LME copper contract was trading at a $181.50 premium to the three-month forward, indicating scarce near-term availability.

Aluminium fell 0.6% to $3,035.50 per ton, close to the eight-month low it touched on Monday. Some easing in passage restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz has reconnected Gulf smelters to the world, taking aluminium prices down, Panmure Liberum said.

New supply from Indonesia is also ramping up, with exports topping 150,000 tons in August.

Zinc lost 0.4% to $3,741.50, lead rose 0.6% to $1,894.50, nickel was flat at $15,620 and tin eased 0.2% to $53,000.

headline: SE Fruits and Vegetable to refile IPO application with additional disclosures
summary: SE Fruits and Vegetable Limited will withdraw its existing initial public offering (IPO) application and submit a fresh one with additional disclosures about the transition of its underlying business from a partnership to a public limited company, the company said on Tuesday.“The Board of Directors of SE Fruits and Vegetable Limited has decided to withdraw the Company’s current IPO application and submit a fresh application after incorporating additional disclosures into the prospectus,” the company said in a statement.“The additional disclosures will provide further information regarding the transition of the underlying business from a partnership organisation, operating since 1998, to the newly incorporated Public Limited Company in 2026,” it added.Sources familiar with the matter said the application was being withdrawn after concerns emerged over disclosures that had not been adequately included in the IPO documents.The omissions came to the attention of regulators, prompting the company to resubmit its application with the required information, the sources toldBusiness Recorder.“The Board considers the resubmission to be in the interests of transparency, regulatory compliance, investor protection and informed investment decision-making,” SE Fruits said, adding that it remained committed to accessing Pakistan’s capital markets.“The withdrawal is a procedural step and does not represent an abandonment of the company’s IPO plans. SE Fruits remains committed to accessing Pakistan’s capital markets and intends to reapply after completing the revised prospectus and applicable regulatory process,” it said.SE Fruits, Vegs secures SECP approval for IPOSE Fruits and Vegetables Limited, formerly known as Shaheen Enterprises, is a Punjab-based horticulture exporter specialising in mangoes, citrus (kinnow), and potatoes, along with other agricultural produce.As of FY2026, SE Fruits and Vegetables reported a topline of approximately $7.6 million and export revenue of about $4 million. Its net revenue for FY2026 was Rs2.133 billion, with a profit after tax of Rs303.8 million, and it has been debt-free since FY2024. The company held less than a 2% market share in national fruit and vegetable exports in FY2026.In 2026, SE Fruits and Vegetables became the first fresh fruit and vegetable company to prepare for listing on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) through an Initial Public Offering (IPO). The IPO aims to raise between Rs1.2 billion and Rs1.92 billion to fund working capital, expand processing and export operations, establish international offices in the UAE and Uzbekistan, and invest in enterprise resource planning, asset-tracking systems, and solar energy.

article_text:
England on Tuesday named their squads for November’s white-ball tour of Australia, with all-rounder Jacob Bethell returning from a knee injury as they step up preparations for next year’s One Day International World Cup.

Bethell, who was injured during England’s ODI series win over India in July, has been selected in both the ODI and T20 squads.

Jofra Archer also returns for the ODI series after being rested for this month’s tri-series in Pakistan, while uncapped bowler Eddie Jack and 18-year-old wicketkeeper-batter Thomas Rew are among those who earned their maiden senior England call-ups in the T20 squad.

Wicketkeeper-batter Phil Salt returns after a quad injury ruled him out of England’s 3-0 T20 series sweep of Sri Lanka last month.

Wicketkeeper-batter Jos Buttler remains sidelined as he begins rehabilitation following hamstring surgery, while fast bowler Saqib Mahmood misses out with a knee injury.

England increase central contracts to record 39

Archer and fellow quicks Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker and Josh Tongue will leave the tour after the three-match ODI series as England manage their workloads ahead of the Test tour of South Africa in December.

The Australia series forms part of England’s build-up to next year’s ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

article_text:
MUMBAI: Borrowing costs for the most liquid part of India’s state government bond curve breached the 8% handle for the first time in over six years on Tuesday, according to traders, tracking a sharp spike in central government yields and weakening investor appetite.

Indian states raised over 300 billion rupees ($3.15 billion) through a sale of bonds, of which 9- to 10-year state bonds were sold in the 8.03%-8.10% range.

This is the first time since April 2020 that yields on state government bonds with a 10-year maturity have broken 8%.

Yields on other ultra-long papers were between 8.14% and 8.21%.

“The rise in state debt yields reflects a combination of elevated crude oil prices, tighter liquidity conditions, and open market sales,” said Harsimran Sahni, associate director and head of treasury at Anand Rathi Global Finance.

Last week, states raised funds through 9- to 10-year bonds in the 7.91%-7.93% band.

The benchmark 10-year 6.94% 2036 bond yield was at 7.36% on Tuesday, up from 7.19% last week.

India bonds rise as investors see value after 10-year yield nears 7.40%

The yield spread of 10-year state bonds over central government bonds has compressed from around 75 basis points to about 65 bps in the last two months, and “we expect it to remain in the 55-70 bps range in the near term,” Sahni added.

Indian states aim to raise over 3.6 trillion rupees through bonds this quarter, after raising 5 trillion rupees in the first half of the fiscal.

MUMBAI: The flagship firm of India’s Adani group, Adani Enterprises, plans to raise around 20 billion rupees ($210 million) through the sale of short-duration bonds, two merchant bankers directly aware of the transaction said on Tuesday.

“The company would look for an issuance of below five-year maturity, and may aim to complete the sale within this quarter,” one of the bankers said.

The funds are being raised for general corporate purposes, the bankers said, adding that the details are yet to be finalised.

The bankers requested anonymity as they are not authorised to speak to the media. The company did not reply to a Reuters email seeking comment.

India regulator presses ahead against Hindenburg, others in Adani case, sources say

The fundraise comes after CareEdge Ratings last week upgraded the firm’s long-term rating by one notch to AA from AA-, reflecting the strengthened financial risk profile of the firm.

At the start of 2026, the company had raised 10 billion rupees, which was its third public issue of debt, after tapping that route first in September 2024 and later in July 2025.

The company last tapped private corporate debt in October 2025, when it raised 10 billion rupees through the sale of bonds maturing in two years and six months at a semi-annual coupon of 8.70%.

He struck twice in one over with the newft ball after already having taken two wickets on Monday and then breaking through South Africa’s stoic early fightback on Tuesday.

The 35-year-old Hazlewood also removed the last batsman to ensure the victory in the first clash between the teams since South Africa upset Australia in last year’s World Test Championship final at Lord’s in London.

South Africa held out for the first 110 minutes of Tuesday’s play before a legside delivery from Hazlewood was edged by Wiaan Mulder and snagged by a diving catch from wicketkeeper Alex Carey.

Mulder and Aiden Markram resumed at 102-4 overnight and the pair extended the fifth-wicket partnership to a patient 69 runs off 205 balls before Hazlewood’s breakthrough with Mulder making 29.

Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw, who was the man of the match for Australia with the bat, then took a second Test wicket when Kyle Verreynne quickly followed Mulder back to the change room with a reckless shot that saw him caught at slip by Steve Smith without scoring.

South Africa were 166-6 at lunch and added 25 runs before the new ball was taken but crumbled quickly thereafter.

Jansen was bowled by Hazlewood for 35 and three balls later Simon Harmer followed as he brushed the ball through to Carey with his glove.

Markram then fell after a patient 75 off 237 balls, edging Mitch Starc’s delivery off his pads to be caught behind but was only given out after a television review.

Hazlewood thencompleted the win as tailender Anrich Nortje popped up the ball to short midwicket for Nathan Lyon to catch.

Former Australia captain Smith, who did not field in Monday’s late session after a blow to the head while batting, returned to action on Tuesday.

“Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning,” a statement said.

MUMBAI: Indian government bonds snapped a four-session falling streak on Tuesday, after the yield rising to a three-year high attracted investors back to the market.

A policy rate hike and liquidity withdrawal by the central bank had pushed the benchmark bond yield up by 20 basis points over four sessions. The 6.94% 2036 bond ended at 7.3655% against 7.3857% in the previous session.

The rupee outperformed its regional peers and ended 0.5% up against the dollar at 95.28, boosted by new central bank measures to alleviate pressure on the Asian currency and likely spot market intervention that magnified their impact.

“The base case is that the 10-year bond yield has provided support in the 7.40% ranges, however, any further OMO (open market operation) sale could push the 10-year benchmark yield towards the 7.60–7.65% range,” said Harsimran Sahni, associate director and head of treasury at Anand Rathi Global Finance.

India’s state borrowing costs spike to over six-year high as demand fades

The RBI raised its key policy rate by 25 basis points last week and changed its policy stance, hinting at more hikes in coming months. The central bank has also announced currency market measures that cloud the outlook for banking system liquidity and impact banks’ treasury operations.

Bets of a December rate increase have hardened after consumer inflation accelerated to 5.54% in September, while the benchmark Brent crude contract held above the $105 per barrel mark.

Bond gains were curbed by hefty supply.

Indian states raised over 300 billion rupees through bonds while the Reserve Bank of India sold notes worth 250 billion rupees through an open market operation. New Delhi is sue to sell benchmark note worth 340 billion rupees on Friday.

Traders awaited US inflation data due on Wednesday for cues on the Federal Reserve’s moves.

Overnight indexed swap rates eased, tracking bond yields and a pullback in US Treasury yields.

The one-year OIS rate ended at 6.3350%, while the two-year rate closed at 6.5150%, and the most liquid five-year rate settled lower at 6.74%.

PM Shehbaz Sharif announced the government will set wheat prices after provincial consultations, aiming for fair farmer returns and consumer affordability, while emphasizing agricultural growth and food security.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Tuesday that the government will announce the wheat price after consultations with the provinces, stressing that the decision must ensure fair returns for farmers while keeping wheat affordable for consumers.

Chairing the first meeting of the National Agriculture and Food Security Council (NAFSC) in Islamabad on Tuesday, the prime minister said determining the wheat price before the start of sowing was essential to compensate farmers adequately for their efforts.

He said the country had sufficient wheat stocks to meet domestic requirements and warned that those involved in hoarding the commodity would not be given any concession.

The prime minister said agriculture was the backbone of Pakistan’s economy and had the potential to put the country on a growth trajectory in the short term.

He said the federal government would extend all possible support to the provinces to promote agricultural development, adding that providing farmers with fertilisers at affordable rates, quality seeds, modern machinery and equipment and technical expertise for efficient water use was a priority.

Shehbaz also emphasised ensuring fair prices for crops, particularly for small and medium-sized farmers.

Highlighting the potential of the livestock sector, he said it could significantly boost the country’s exports. He added that the government was taking steps to increase exports of Pakistani halal meat.

The prime minister appreciated Punjab’s initiatives for farmers, including aquaculture, shrimp farming and direct subsidies through the Kisan Card. He also acknowledged the Sindh government’s efforts to support farmers and improve access to facilities.

During the meeting, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif and Sindh Food Minister Makhdoom Mahboob-uz-Zaman briefed participants on their respective provincial governments’ initiatives for farmers and agricultural development.

The meeting was also briefed on measures to promote agriculture in Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, federal ministers Rana Tanveer Hussain, Musadik Malik, Jam Kamal Khan, Ahsan Iqbal and Attaullah Tarar, among other federal officials and advisers, attended the meeting.

A constitutional petition seeks the immediate recovery of non-functional KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, allegedly abducted from his official residence, citing grave constitutional and human rights violations.

A constitutional petition has been filed in the Peshawar High Court (PHC) seeking the immediate recovery of non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, whose brother alleges he was abducted from the Chief Minister’s House and is being held in illegal custody.

The petition was filed by Muhammad Aamir, the non-functional KP chief minister’s brother, who urged the court to take immediate action, order Afridi’s recovery and direct authorities to produce him before the court, read a statement shared by Sohail Afridi’s Facebook page.

The petitioner alleged that armed and masked men took away the elected chief minister in the presence of the Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Peshawar. He said the alleged abduction and detention violated the Constitution, the law and fundamental human rights.

The petition maintains that Afridi’s life and liberty are at serious risk and that his continued detention, along with the lack of information about his whereabouts, raises grave constitutional concerns. It cites Articles 4, 9, 10 and 14 of the Constitution.

The petitioner has asked the court to direct the CCPO Peshawar to submit complete details of the alleged incident and the security arrangements in place at the time. He has also sought an explanation of his brother’s whereabouts, who is holding him and under what legal authority.

The petition further seeks an independent and impartial investigation into the alleged abduction, the identification of those involved and action against them in accordance with the law.

It also asks the court to order the immediate preservation of CCTV footage, security records and other evidence related to the incident, and direct police officials to submit a detailed report on steps taken to recover the chief minister.

The petitioner has urged the high court to ensure Afridi’s safety, liberty and protection, warning that any delay in addressing the matter could endanger his life. He has requested that the petition be fixed for an urgent hearing.

Pakistan's PM urged Europe to expand legal migration for skilled workers, citing mutual benefits and anti-smuggling efforts. An EU Commissioner praised Pakistan's significant reduction in illegal migration.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called for expanding legal migration opportunities for Pakistani skilled workers and professionals in Europe, saying such pathways could help meet European labour-market needs while protecting prospective migrants from smuggling networks.

The prime minister made these remarks during a meeting with European Union Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner, who called on him in Islamabad during his first visit to Pakistan, the PM Office said.

Highlighting Pakistan’s efforts to combat irregular migration, migrant smuggling and human trafficking through legislative reforms, stronger institutions, effective enforcement and international cooperation, Shehbaz emphasized: “Efforts to address irregular migration should be complemented by practical opportunities for safe, orderly, and regular migration.”

The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening its partnership with the European Union and cooperation across all pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan 2019. Migration and mobility are among the plan’s eight pillars.

Commissioner Brunner appreciated the measures taken by Pakistan and the cooperation extended by its government.

He expressed confidence that these efforts would help expand legal migration pathways and promote mutually beneficial labour mobility between Pakistan and the European Union.

Earlier, during a meeting with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in Islamabad, European Commissioner Brunner praised Pakistan’s measures to combat illegal migration.

Brunner said Pakistan’s effective measures have resulted in a commendable 64% reduction in illegal migration to Europe.

He also commended the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) for demonstrating professional capabilities despite limited resources. He said reducing illegal migration will open up pathways for legal migration.

Naqvi said Pakistan has adopted a zero-tolerance policy against illegal migration. “Following a 64% reduction in illegal migration, our next target is to eliminate it completely,” he said.

The minister stressed the need for Pakistan and the European Union to work together to completely eliminate illegal migration.

During the meeting, the two sides discussed promoting legal migration between Pakistan and the European Union and expanding opportunities for skilled workers.

Both sides agreed to enhance cooperation in border security and promote legal immigration. They also agreed to further strengthen collaboration in migration, institutional cooperation and border management.

Around 7,900 people died or disappeared on migration routes in 2025, taking the total dead and missing since 2014 beyond 80,000, the United Nations’ migration agency said in a statement on April 21.

The UN’s International Organization for Migration said people were being forced into dangerous, irregular journeys when safe pathways were out of reach, and urged countries to find the political will to save more lives on migration routes.

The deaths or disappearance of around “7,900 people were documented on global migration routes worldwide in 2025”, the IOM said.

The IOM’s Missing Migrants Project “has documented more than 80,000 deaths and disappearances during migration since 2014,” the agency said.

“While these figures represent only the lowest boundary of the true number of affected people, they nonetheless underscore the need for urgent action to end migrant deaths and address the complex needs of families left behind,” said the IOM.

Pakistan Army has successfully test-fired the extended-range version of its Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile, the military’s media wing said on Tuesday.

According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the weapon system is equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics, enabling it to engage targets with high precision.

The ISPR said the missile’s unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features enable it to defeat enemy missile defence systems, while its extended range further enhances the army’s capability to engage targets deep inside enemy territory.

The commander appreciated the dedication and technical expertise of the scientists and engineers, the statement added.

President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, and the services chiefs congratulated the scientists and engineers on the successful test launch.

Separately, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the test, describing it as a significant development in the country’s defence sector.

He said Pakistan Army scientists and engineers had achieved a commendable feat.

BENGALURU: An influential Hindu nationalist group close to India’s ruling party urged the government on Tuesday to block Elon Musk’s Starlink from launching satellite internet services in the country, citing national security concerns.

Starlink’s four-year wait to launch in India has come under renewed scrutiny after Musk last week accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government and billionaire Mukesh Ambani of stalling its entry to favour Ambani’s Reliance Jio.

India’s communications ministry said last week that security assessments were under way for Starlink and rival satellite ventures backed by Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel. It described suggestions the approval process was unfair or discriminatory as “baseless and misconceived”.

The call for Starlink’s ban came from Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM), the economic wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the Hindu nationalist organisation that is the ideological parent of Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

India rejects monopoly claim after Musk accuses Ambani of blocking Starlink launch

SJM also linked its demand to trade tensions with the US. If Washington imposes high tariffs on Indian imports “in the name of national security, then India is certainly within its rights to block Starlink based on its genuine national security concerns,” national co-convenor Ashwani Mahajan said in a statement.

Starlink’s technology could make it difficult for authorities to restrict internet services during security emergencies and ensure Indian internet traffic passes through domestic infrastructure, Mahajan added.

SJM has influenced Indian policy in recent years, notably pushing for rules to protect small traders from US-owned e-commerce firms Amazon and Walmart’s Flipkart.

SpaceX, Starlink’s parent company, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Market with more than a billion internet users

Starlink is seeking to launch in a country with more than a billion internet subscribers. Alongside Starlink, satellite ventures backed by Reliance Jio and Bharti are awaiting final clearances to begin services.

Musk has repeatedly taunted Ambani on X, questioning why Starlink still lacked a licence despite what he said were years of compliance with Indian requirements.

“Is Ambani the real boss of India?” he posted last week, as he accused the rival billionaire of stalling Starlink’s entry.

WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said late on Monday he did not believe that China and Russia were helping Iran “at all,” adding that Moscow and Beijing had “too much to lose” if they enabled Tehran.

Trump said on Truth Social that he had seen comments from his critics and opponents that China and Russia were helping Iran.

“If they are, it’s at a very low level, but I don’t believe they are at all. They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast,” Trump wrote.

Trump said in July he trusted China and Russia not to help Tehran in the Iran war, but warned that if they did get involved “it would be very bad for them.”

The United States and Iran have been at war since February 28, when ​the US and Israel attacked Iran and Tehran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and ​Israeli attacks on Lebanon have since killed thousands and displaced millions.

Trump says US will not attack Iran before midterm elections in November

Trump has previously described Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin as “neutral” during the Iran war.

Iranian drone attacks on CIA facilities in the Gulf have prompted US intelligence analysts to investigate whether Russia provided targeting information or ​advanced drone technology. European foreign ministers pressed the case in a March meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The Washington Post and the Wall Street Journal that month reported that Russia was providing Iran with targeting information.

Moscow and Beijing maintain close ties with Tehran. Russia has said the Iran war could lead to a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. Beijing has condemned Washington’s attacks on Tehran as a brazen violation of Iran’s sovereignty.

Last month, Trump warned Xi against providing support to Iran when the Chinese leader visited Washington, and received assurances that China would not do so, the US ambassador to China said at the time.

Trump defends Russia diesel deal as lawmakers from both parties complain

The warning came amid reports that China had supplied Iran with shoulder-fired ​air-defense missile launchers and that Tehran had found ways to evade sanctions on its oil sales with Chinese ​help.

In September, Trump brushed aside a report that Iran acquired satellite images of a base in Jordan from Chinese entities before an attack that killed three US troops there in July.

Pakistan's Finance Minister reaffirmed national ownership of IMF-supported reforms in taxation, energy, SOEs, and pensions, stressing sustained implementation for economic growth and public welfare.

Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb reaffirmed on Tuesday Pakistan’s ownership of taxation, energy, state-owned enterprise (SOE) and pension reforms under the IMF-supported programme, stressing that sustained implementation was essential to achieve lasting economic growth and public welfare.

The development came as the minister highlighted debt management and fiscal reforms at a panel on Mitigating Sovereign Risks in Market-Access Countries on the sidelines of the World Bank Group–IMF Annual Meetings 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand, according to a Finance Division statement.

“The Finance minister reaffirmed national ownership of taxation, energy, state-owned enterprises and pension reforms under the IMF-supported programme. He stressed the sustained reform implementation to translate macroeconomic stability into sustainable growth and public welfare,” the statement read.

The minister further highlighted Pakistan’s progress in fiscal consolidation, reducing inflation and rebuilding foreign exchange reserves.

“He emphasised revenue mobilisation, tax administration reforms, expenditure restraint and privatisation to strengthen economic resilience,” the statement read.

Aurangzeb outlined debt management measures to lower financing costs, extend maturities and reduce rollover risks. He noted that renewed market access supports a strategy to improve the external debt profile without increasing the overall size.

Finance minister discusses Mashreq Bank’s expansion

Federal minister Aurangzeb also met with Mashreq Bank’s senior management to discuss its expanding presence in Pakistan, a separate Finance Division statement said.

The minister highlighted macroeconomic gains and renewed market access, reaffirming support for Mashreq’s expansion and sustainable growth. He reviewed digital banking growth and opportunities to advance financial inclusion through technology and microfinance.

“Discussion also covered expanding offshore service operations, drawing on Pakistan’s skilled workforce. The meeting explored digital accounts for overseas Pakistanis, foreign-currency products and wider outreach across the GCC.” the statement read.

He also discussed collaboration on tokenisation, blockchain, and digital assets within Pakistan’s evolving regulatory framework. He reviewed potential support for Sukuk, further Panda bond issuance and innovative financing under Pakistan’s medium-term debt strategy.

A Saudi-led coalition urged civilians on Tuesday to evacuate the Yemen Oil Company’s Sabah central station in the capital Sanaa ahead of a planned military operation.

A statement from the coalition’s joint forces command identified the site on a map and said civilians should leave the area for their own safety.

A spokesperson for Yemen’s Houthis, Yahya Saree, warned that any strikes on Sanaa would be met with a “harsh and painful” response in the Saudi capital Riyadh.

Houthis also warned employees and civilians near Saudi Aramco oil facilities to evacuate and stay away, saying the facilities were legitimate targets for their forces.

Houthis claim attack targeting Riyadh airport with ballistic missile

Fighting has escalated between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis, who have been attacking Saudi airports and oil facilities since last week in a spillover from the wider regional conflagration between the US and Iran.

Saudi Arabia has in recent weeks launched strikes against the Houthis and is backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

The conflict has disrupted air travel in Saudi Arabia, with Riyadh airport remaining closed after a deadly missile strike on Saturday claimed by the Houthis.

LONDON: Britain’s Prince William turned one of London’s most famous thoroughfares, The Mall leading to Buckingham Palace, into a temporary cricket pitch on Tuesday, where he was joined by some of the game’s biggest names to promote his Earthshot climate prize.

The wide red-paved promenade in the heart of the city is more often seen as the setting for grand royal processions and patriotic flag-waving celebrations.

But on Tuesday, William picked up a cricket bat for an informal game with current and former international players including ex-Indian captain Sourav Ganguly, West Indies legend Brian Lara and England captain Joe Root.

Against the palatial backdrop, William - dressed in a shirt and sweater - clubbed away a series of gentle deliveries from Ganguly and posed for selfies with onlookers.

“He batted alright,” said Ganguly when asked for his verdict on the prince’s skills.

The event was designed to celebrate the ties between Britain and India - two passionate cricketing nations - as India prepares to host the annual summit and awards ceremony of William’s Earthshot Prize next month.

The prize, founded in 2020, honours five winners with £1 million ($1.32 million) each to scale solutions aimed at repairing the planet.

headline: Textile body urges PM to retain export facilitation scheme for yarns, fabrics
